belief: People get tired of repeating things for me.
origins: Asking “What?” again and again, or needing text or large print, can create guilt. Some nod along to avoid asking, and miss much. Others withdraw to avoid being a bother.
teaches: “Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.” “Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak.” Love is “patient” and “kind” (1 Corinthians 13:4). Most people would rather repeat themselves than see you left out. When someone is truly impatient, that reflects their limits, not your worth. You can help them by telling them what works for you: face me, speak clearly, write it down.
self_statements: I am a burden to talk to.
I will just pretend I heard.
They would rather not talk to me.
errors: Believing people either hear me easily or are annoyed.
Feeling like a bother and concluding that I am.
questions: What have people actually said or shown?
What helps me understand: facing me, writing, quiet rooms?
How could I tell people what helps?
What do I miss when I pretend to hear?
What does Scripture say about patience and burden-bearing?
truth: Asking for what I need is an act of respect for myself and others. Most people want to include me. I can tell them what helps, and I can be gracious with myself.
hw_truths: I can tell people what helps.
log: Each week, note one time you asked for what you needed.
actions: Try, “It helps me if you face me and speak slowly.”
prayer: Lord, I do not want to wear people out. Give me courage to ask for what I need, and surround me with patient, loving people. Amen.
